On 18 June the council executive board is asked to remove phone booking from all seven community venues from September. The officers' report gives one reason: staff should not have to enter the details in two flows. That is a fair thing to want. It is not yet a reason to make the change permanent.

The administration's objection to keeping both routes is double administration, and I take it at face value: it is not a claim that people who ring are lazy or expensive. The board is being asked to close a channel for good on the strength of an inconvenience the documents put no number on. That is thin ground for making the change permanent.

Öppna beslut proposes a six-month trial in all seven venues with both booking routes kept open. During it, the administration records the time each booking route takes and asks users to say, voluntarily, why they chose the phone or the web. We make no claim to have funded or costed that trial. Postpone the permanent switch and run the six months with both routes open. When the trial has produced figures, decide whether a channel should be removed, changed or kept.
